messages:
kevin.k: Quick post — profiler spike on canary today. noticed batching stalls when requests hit mixed-variant compat sets. logs attached below.

sarah.l: can you paste the hotspot? is it queue wait or kernel launch?

kevin.k: looks like queue wait plus a KV prefetch stall. snippet from trace: 
```
queue_wait_ms: 14.2
kv_prefetch_ms: 36.7
batch_size: 4
variant_selected: mv/quant8-fallback
compat_check_ms: 5.1
```

alex_m: 36ms KV prefetch sounds high — which path? cold cache or prewarm miss?

kevin.k: cold for some prefixes, but prefetch logic currently tries to pull whole prefix into KV before batch formation. that blocks formation when mixed-models have different key schemas.

prashant: hmm that explains slower batch formation. our batching heuristic waits up to token_budget or timeout. if one request is waiting on KV, it stalls others that could have been formed into a fast homogeneous batch.

iris: idea: make prefetch nonblocking — start batch formation with available requests and let KV fill async, evicting requests whose model variant needs different KV layout to a separate compat queue.

alex_m: +1. we already have compat sets per model family. what if we push prefetch into a separate task and mark request as "kv_pending". batcher can form based on core compat tag and token_budget. when kv_ready fires, we either merge remaining tokens or treat as streaming append.

kevin.k: prototype config I tried: 
```
batcher:
  token_budget_target: 256
  max_delay_ms: 12
  compat_mode: strict_by_model_family
  kv_prefetch: async
  kv_prefetch_timeout_ms: 40
  separate_kv_queue: true
```

kevin.k: with that, queue_wait dropped to 3-5ms, kv_prefetch still ~30ms but didn't block. overall tail latency p95 for short prompts improved ~18%.

prashant: nice. tradeoff: might increase duplicate KV pulls when batch merges happen across variants? need to watch extra bandwidth + cache churn.

iris: also need to adjust kernel selection fallback. if a batch contains mixed precision variants, kernel selector currently picks conservative kernel causing perf regressions. maybe select per-subbatch kernel when possible.

alex_m: per-subbatch kernel selection seems doable: runtime supports multiple kernel launches per dispatch. downside is more kernel launch overhead; but our traces show kernel launch cost << waiting on kv.

perf-bot: perf regression alert suppressed for this canary due to targeted kv-prefetch experiment — baseline p95 delta -17% (improvement). CI perf tests queued.

kevin.k: next steps: (1) make kv_prefetch async + separate queue, (2) update batcher to compose batches by compat tag ignoring kv_pending, (3) implement per-subbatch kernel selection, (4) run 24h canary with traffic mix. i'll open an RFC and a canary config.

sarah.l: add a metric for "kv-prefetch-duplicates" and "compat-merged-batches" so we can quantify extra pulls and merging wins.

prashant: i'll review RFC and sketch queue policy change. quick note: make sure token_budget math accounts for async kv — don't overfill batch if kv_required tokens still coming.

kevin.k: noted. attaching a small flamegraph and perf trace link: https://perf.internal/redwood/1780000001-trace

iris: thanks — will sync after RFC. :thumbsup:
